laws.title: Illegal Firearms Possession
laws.subtitle: National Firearms Act, not a registry of ordinary guns
laws.fullDescription: There is no federal registry of ordinary rifles, shotguns, and handguns. The National Firearms Act covers machine guns, destructive devices, short-barreled rifles and shotguns, silencers, and certain other concealable firearms called “any other weapons.” On October 9, 2026, ATF stopped enforcing the NFA registration, tax-stamp, and prior-approval rules for short-barreled rifles, short-barreled shotguns, silencers, and any-other-weapons. Machine guns and destructive devices remain fully under the NFA. State and local laws still apply.
laws.penalty: 26 U.S.C. 5871: a fine of not more than $10,000, imprisonment for not more than 10 years, or both, for a violation of that chapter.
laws.sourceLabel: ATF, Update to NFA Transfer Guidance; 26 U.S.C. 5871

quiz.q: Primary area for Illegal Firearms Possession in United States?
quiz.explanation: This law falls under criminal law.

laws.title: Drug Trafficking
laws.subtitle: Controlled Substances Act
laws.fullDescription: Trafficking a controlled substance is a federal crime under the Controlled Substances Act. The penalty depends on the substance, the quantity, and the person's record. This card does not restate the schedules.
laws.penalty: Set by the Controlled Substances Act. It depends on the drug, the quantity, and prior convictions.

quiz.q: Primary area for Drug Trafficking in United States?
quiz.explanation: This law falls under criminal law.

laws.title: Human Trafficking
laws.subtitle: 18 U.S.C. 1591 and related statutes
laws.fullDescription: Using force, fraud, or coercion to obtain labor or a commercial sex act is a federal crime. Sex trafficking of a minor does not require proof of force. The Department of Justice lists the main statutes, including 18 U.S.C. 1591.
laws.penalty: Set out in 18 U.S.C. chapter 77. This card does not restate every maximum.
laws.sourceLabel: U.S. Department of Justice, Human Trafficking Key Legislation

quiz.q: Primary area for Human Trafficking in United States?
quiz.explanation: This law falls under criminal law.

laws.title: Corruption and Bribery
laws.subtitle: 18 U.S.C. 201
laws.fullDescription: 18 U.S.C. 201 makes it a crime to give or accept anything of value to influence an official act of a federal public official. A bribe under subsection (b) is punishable by a fine, imprisonment for not more than 15 years, or both. An illegal gratuity under subsection (c) has a lower maximum.
laws.penalty: Bribery under 18 U.S.C. 201(b): a fine, up to 15 years, or both.

quiz.q: Primary area for Corruption and Bribery in United States?
quiz.explanation: This law falls under criminal law.

laws.title: Drink-Driving
laws.subtitle: 0.08 BAC, except Utah at 0.05
laws.fullDescription: Driving at a blood alcohol concentration of 0.08 or higher is illegal in every state, the District of Columbia, and Puerto Rico, except Utah, where the limit is 0.05. Penalties, and any lower limits for drivers under 21 or commercial drivers, are set by state law.

quiz.q: Primary area for Drink-Driving in United States?
quiz.explanation: This law falls under traffic law.

laws.title: Minimum Wage
laws.subtitle: Fair Labor Standards Act — federal floor
laws.fullDescription: The federal minimum wage for covered nonexempt employees is $7.25 per hour, in effect since July 24, 2009. If a state or local rate is higher, the worker is entitled to the higher rate.
laws.penalty: Back wages under the Fair Labor Standards Act. Enforcement amounts are set by the Department of Labor.
laws.sourceLabel: U.S. Department of Labor, Wages and the Fair Labor Standards Act

quiz.q: Primary area for Minimum Wage in United States?
quiz.explanation: This law falls under labor law.

laws.title: Illegal Deforestation
laws.subtitle: No single nationwide clearing permit
laws.fullDescription: There is no single federal permit that covers every clearing of trees on private land. Cutting timber and other uses of National Forest System land are regulated by the Forest Service. State and local rules can also apply.
laws.penalty: Depends on who owns the land and which statute applies. This card does not state a nationwide sentence.

quiz.q: Primary area for Illegal Deforestation in United States?
quiz.explanation: This law falls under environmental law.

laws.title: Data Protection
laws.subtitle: No single federal consumer privacy statute
laws.fullDescription: There is no single federal law that covers all collection and sale of personal data by businesses. Federal privacy rules are sector by sector. The Privacy Act of 1974 covers records federal agencies keep about individuals.
laws.penalty: Depends on the sector statute. This card does not state one nationwide fine.

quiz.q: Primary area for Data Protection in United States?
quiz.explanation: This law falls under criminal law.

laws.title: Visa Overstay
laws.subtitle: Unlawful presence is not one flat fine
laws.fullDescription: Staying in the United States after the period of authorized stay can make a person inadmissible if they leave and try to return. How long the bar lasts depends on how long the person was unlawfully present and on their status. This is not a single fine that applies to every overstay.
laws.penalty: Inadmissibility bars depend on the length of unlawful presence. Confirm the current rule with USCIS or a lawyer.
laws.sourceLabel: USCIS, Unlawful Presence and Bars to Admissibility

quiz.q: Primary area for Visa Overstay in United States?
quiz.explanation: This law falls under criminal law.

laws.title: Child Custody
laws.subtitle: State courts, not one federal family code
laws.fullDescription: Child custody and visitation are decided under state law. There is no single United States family code for custody. When more than one state is involved, the Parental Kidnapping Prevention Act, 28 U.S.C. 1738A, tells courts which state's custody order to respect.
laws.penalty: Enforcement is under state law. Interstate disputes also follow 28 U.S.C. 1738A.

quiz.q: Primary area for Child Custody in United States?
quiz.explanation: This law falls under criminal law.
